L17: Based on the well-known Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), Singular Spectrum Analysis (SSA) has been widely employed for time series analysis and forecasting in decomposing the original series into a sum of components. As such, each 1-D signal can be represented with varying trend, oscillations and noise for easy enhancement of the signal.
L18: Taking each spectral signature in Hyperspectral Imaging (HSI) as a 1-D signal, SSA has been successfully applied for signal decomposition and noise removal whilst preserving the discriminating power of the spectral profile. Two well-known remote sensing datasets for land cover analysis, AVIRIS 92AV3C and Salinas C, are used for performance assessment.
L19: Experimental results using Support Vector Machine (SVM) in pixel based classification have indicated that SSA has suppressed the noise in significantly improving the classification accuracy.

L0@P0: SINGULAR SPECTRUM ANALYSIS FOR EFFECTIVE NOISE REMOVAL AND
L1@P0: IMPROVED DATA CLASSIFICATION IN HYPERSPECTRAL IMAGING
L2@P0: Jaime Zabalza, Jinchang Ren, Stephen Marshall
L3@P0: {j.zabalza, jinchang.ren, stephen.marshall}@strath.ac.uk
L4@P0: Centre for excellence in Signal and Image Processing, Dept. of Electronic and Electrical Engineering,
L5@P0: University of Strathclyde, Glasgow, G1 1XW, U.K.
L6@P0: ABSTRACT
L7@P0: Based on the well-known Singular Value Decomposition
L8@P0: (SVD), Singular Spectrum Analysis (SSA) has been widely
L9@P0: employed for time series analysis and forecasting in
L10@P0: decomposing the original series into a sum of components.
L11@P0: As such, each 1-D signal can be represented with varying
L12@P0: trend, oscillations and noise for easy enhancement of the
L13@P0: signal. Taking each spectral signature in Hyperspectral
L14@P0: Imaging (HSI) as a 1-D signal, SSA has been successfully
L15@P0: applied for signal decomposition and noise removal whilst
L16@P0: preserving the discriminating power of the spectral profile.
L17@P0: Two well-known remote sensing datasets for land cover
L18@P0: analysis, AVIRIS 92AV3C and Salinas C, are used for
L19@P0: performance assessment. Experimental results using Support
L20@P0: Vector Machine (SVM) in pixel based classification have
L21@P0: indicated that SSA has suppressed the noise in significantly
L22@P0: improving the classification accuracy.
L23@P0: Index Terms— Singular Spectrum Analysis (SSA),
L24@P0: Hyperspectral Imaging (HSI), feature extraction, noise
L25@P0: removal, data classification.
L26@P0: 1. INTRODUCTION
L27@P0: Hyperspectral Imaging (HSI) has powerful capabilities in
L28@P0: data analysis and mining, as images are captured in both
L29@P0: spatial and spectral domains, providing 2-D scenes where
L30@P0: pixels present high resolution and wide range spectral
L31@P0: information. For all this, HSI is used in emerging data
L32@P0: analysis as food quality or verification of documents [1-2].
L33@P0: In HSI, classification of the pixels from a scene can be
L34@P0: accurate thanks to the dimension of features (spectral bands)
L35@P0: provided, especially for powerful classifiers as Support
L36@P0: Vector Machine (SVM) [3-4]. Nonetheless, since HSI data
L37@P0: is prone to noise, it is encouraging the idea of a potential
L38@P0: decomposition in the spectral domain of the pixels so noise
L39@P0: can be avoided. Regarding this decomposition idea, an
L40@P0: inspiring research for us is [4], where the Empirical Mode
L41@P0: Decomposition (EMD) technique is applied to the pixels and
L42@P0: briefly evaluated for classification tasks.
L43@P0: Being part of the Hilbert Huang Transform (HHT), an
L44@P0: algorithm used for non-linear and non-stationary data [5],
L45@P0: EMD decomposes a 1-D signal into few components called
L46@P0: Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMFs) for a later reconstruction
L47@P0: by only specific IMFs. Although the reconstruction aim was
L48@P0: to achieve higher accuracy in classification tasks, [4] showed
L49@P0: deterioration. Now, it is turn for Singular Spectrum Analysis
L50@P0: (SSA) technique to be evaluated in a similar way.
L51@P0: 2. THE APPROACH
L52@P0: SSA [6] is a recent technique for time series analysis and
L53@P0: forecasting, but also allowing interesting possibilities in
L54@P0: other applications. SSA is able to decompose an original
L55@P0: series into several independent components that are
L56@P0: interpretable as varying trend, oscillations or noise. In fact,
L57@P0: extraction of trends, smoothing or periodic components are
L58@P0: summarized in [6] as some of the main capabilities of SSA.

L329@P1: 3. DATASET AND EXPERIMENTAL RESULTS
L330@P1: Our experiments, carried out in Matlab environment, are
L331@P1: described by sequential stages. These are: (1) data
L332@P1: description and conditioning, (2) experimental settings and
L333@P1: classification, (3) results in noise removal, and (4) results in
L334@P1: data classification.
L335@P1: 3.1. Data Description and Conditioning
L336@P1: Two datasets for remote sensing purposes and with available
L337@P1: ground truth are employed in our experiments (Figs. 1-2).
L338@P1: Fig. 1. One band image at wavelength 667nm (left) and the ground truth
L339@P1-2: maps (right) for the 92AV3C dataset.Firstly, AVIRIS 92AV3C dataset [7] is a sub-scene
L340@P2: from Indiana, USA, with 145×145 pixels in 220 spectral
L341@P2: reflectance bands. It contains 16 labeled classes. Secondly,
L342@P2: AVIRIS Salinas C dataset is a sub-scene extracted from a
L343@P2: largest dataset [8], which was taken over California, USA,
L344@P2: made of 150×150 pixels, 224 spectral bands with 9 classes.
L345@P2: In the conditioning, as recommended by others [3-4, 8],
L346@P2: some bands are removed, so they are finally reduced from
L347@P2: 220 to 200 and 224 to 204, respectively. For the 92AV3C
L348@P2: dataset, only 9 out of the original 16 classes are evaluated,
L349@P2: as stated statistically better by some researchers [3-4].
L350@P2: Fig. 2. One band image wavelength 667nm (left) and the ground truth
L351@P2: maps (right) for the Salinas C dataset.
L352@P2: 3.2. Experimental Settings and Classification
L353@P2: EMD and SSA techniques, by reconstructing pixels in the
L354@P2: HSI scene, are evaluated for noise removal. Also the use of
L355@P2: original pixels is included as Baseline reference.
L356@P2: On one hand, for EMD, the code available in [9] is
L357@P2: implemented, adopting the default stop threshold. For
L358@P2: reconstruction, combinations of the 1
L359@P2: st, 1-2nd and 1-3rd IMFs
L360@P2: are selected as in [4]. On the other hand, for SSA, several
L361@P2: combinations of window L and EVG, shown in Table 1, are
L362@P2: selected to evaluate the corresponding performance.

L374@P2: In order to classify the data, SVM is implemented,
L375@P2: which presents a wide usage in HSI [3-4] and many other
L376@P2: applications, even in embedded systems [10]. LibSVM
L377@P2: library [11] with Gaussian RBF kernel is used here [3-4],
L378@P2: with penalty (c) and gamma (γ) parameters selected every
L379@P2: time through a grid search procedure.
L380@P2: Every experiment is repeated 10 times, varying the subsets for training and testing, in order to avoid systematic
L381@P2: errors. Data partitions are randomly selected by stratified
L382@P2: sampling, using an equal sample rate of 20% for training
L383@P2: each class. Finally, the averaged testing results and
L384@P2: McNemar’s tests [4] over the 10 repetitions are reported.
L385@P2: 3.3. Results in Noise Removal
L386@P2: An original spectral pixel in HSI data can be reconstructed
L387@P2: in an improved way by the main Eigen value components,
L388@P2: discarding those less representatives that usually contain
L389@P2: noise presence.
L390@P2: The SSA reconstruction depends on two parameters.
L391@P2: Firstly, the window size L, which states the total number of
L392@P2: components extracted in the decomposition stage. Secondly,
L393@P2: the Eigen Value Grouping (EVG), which denotes the
L394@P2: selected combination of extracted components used for a
L395@P2: desired reconstruction.

L414@P2: 3.4. Results in Data Classification
L415@P2: Final results are given in Table 2, where it is proved that
L416@P2: SSA de-noising improves the Baseline reference accuracy,
L417@P2: while the EMD usage decreases it, as shown in [4].
L418@P2: McNemar’s tests with respect to the Baseline case, showing
L419@P2: statistical significance at a confidence level of 95% when
L420@P2: │Z│> 1.96, also support the SSA improvement. Only some
L421@P2: cases for Salinas C dataset are below this value because the
L422@P2: improvement is small due to the already high initial
L423@P2-3: accuracy, being difficult to increase it.Further analysis is provided in Table 3, to clearly shown
L424@P3: that the SSA de-noising improvement is detected in terms of
L425@P3: not only Overall Accuracy but also Average and Class by
L426@P3: Class Accuracy, regardless the number of samples per class.
